## Lessons from studied films against code (one auditor, 40 rules; `lessons-vs-code-2026-11-24.md`)
- 30 rules have a check that can fail. Only 14 of those run in the pipeline. 16 sit in checker scripts nothing calls. 8 are notes only.
- Not enforced and most costly: text on a busy picture (judges caught it on 25 of 53 of our frames); the picture arriving 2.5 s before its word; something new on screen about every 7 s (the engine fails only at 20 s).
- Code that works against a lesson: scenes join with a 0.4 s dissolve by default and dust is drawn over pictures; the script checker refuses a pause over 1.5 s after minute two, so a correct 3.0 s chapter pause fails.
- Only a 10 minute film has a measured arc from start to end. None for 8, 15, 20, 30 or 50 minutes.

## Why so much work made so little (Judged)
1. Studies, looks and room drawings ran before the chain existed, so nothing could be tested whole (ADR 0017 says the same).
2. Checks were written and never called by the pipeline.
3. Dozens of long-lived Opus workers each re-read a growing context; the lead's own thread is the largest.
4. The Mac sat at load 42 to 60, so tools timed out and work was repeated.
